title: Pratt Parsing as a Balanced Search & Indexing Structure: State Transitions and Invariant Maintenance
topic: writing about pratt parsing so I remember it
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Pratt parsing, a top-down operator-precedence technique, offers a compact and uniform method for constructing abstract syntax trees (ASTs) for arithmetic expressions. This paper formalises the Pratt parser as a balanced search \& indexing structure, proving that the depth of the produced AST is bounded by $O(\log N)$ where $N$ is the number of tokens, and that the parser preserves the key-ordered invariant of the expression tree. We present a Python implementation that achieves linear time parsing and linear auxiliary space, and we verify the invariants through static AST inspection and formal reasoning. The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261026_170147_writing_about_pratt_parsing_so}.
